activity.title: Assemble builds agents for IT teams that manage enterprise systems like ERPs, CRMs, and HRIS platforms. Even small feature requests can become lengthy IT projects when they touch multiple Salesforce, SAP, and Workday environments built on years of custom logic. In fact, only 48% of enterprise digital initiatives meet or exceed their intended business outcomes. Assemble helps IT teams plan the work, make changes across systems, and roll them back when needed. Founders Aliyan Ishfaq , Shrish Janarthanan , and Shaurnav Ghosh are building Assemble to help IT teams deliver complex transformation projects with both speed and control. Learn more at https://lnkd.in/gV5RR3EJ . Congrats to Aliyan, Shrish, and Shaurnav on the launch! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gte9pwB5 ...more ...more

Second year at Stanford is officially wrapped, and it exceeded every expectation. This year I got to go much deeper into the intersection of bioengineering, hardware, and AI. I joined the Krishnan Lab, where I’ve been working under Atharv Naik on bioelectronic cell-therapy devices, specifically implantable device design, microfluidics, and analog circuits. I’ll be continuing this work over the summer through Stanford’s Electrical Engineering Undergraduate Research grant. I also spent a lot of time building. I competed at hackathons hosted by AGI House, Frontier Tower, and TreeHacks. Built a neural alignment system with Siddharth and Emiliano where OpenBCI EEG headsets combined with Meta's TRIBE v2 neural decoding let multiple people build a 3D world using brain signals, gaze, and speech. At TreeHacks our team ( Mark , Abraham , Gaston , & I) won a prize from Suno for developing an AI music accessibility tool that turns everyday objects into playable instruments using computer vision, real-time MIDI, generative music, and AI coaching. A major academic highlight was taking Tissue Engineering with Dr. Skylar-Scott and Dr. Yang. The class changed how I think about engineered living systems, biofabrication, and the future of therapeutic design. Some other highlights: Drummer of Monarch (a new Stanford band formed at the beginning of the academic year). We have already played 15+ gigs this year. Be sure to catch us next year! Met and learned from awesome people including Andrew Feldman (CEO and co-founder of Cerebras), Fred Swaniker , Roger Federer, and more. Also had some of the most thoughtful conversations of the year with Andrew Kelmanson, Arinze Obiezue , Andrew Carlins , and Shayling Zhao - grateful for the people who have pushed me to think deeper and ask more thoughtful questions. Placed 6th at the Stanford ACM Poker Tournament, sponsored by Jump Trading and Jane Street. Competed in the annual Stanford x Berkeley Poker Tournament. This summer, I’ll be living in The Kernel - a deep tech hacker house in the Bay Area. We are envisioning to create a high-density environment over the summer for people working on ambitious ideas across AI, bioengineering, hardware, robotics, scientific computing, and frontier startups. We’ll be hosting technical build nights, founder dinners, demo sessions, startup/investor gatherings, and small events for builders, researchers, operators, and VCs throughout the summer. If you’re in the Bay Area and are building, backing, or researching at the frontier of technology, reach out. Would love to meet more great people working at the edge of what’s possible. Also excited to attend Y Combinator Summer School this summer, with speakers including Jensen Huang , Sam Altman, Max Hodak, and many more. Looking forward to meeting more founders, builders, and investors working on ambitious ideas. Grateful for the people, ideas, and momentum from this year. Excited for what’s next. ...more

Over the past several months, many of you have followed, supported, encouraged, and engaged with our work — and I’m deeply grateful for the hundreds of new people who have joined this journey. Today, I’m asking you to help us take the next step. We all know the global health funding landscape has changed dramatically. At the same time, the need has not. If anything, it has become even more urgent. One thing I’ve learned is this: people want to give. People want to make a difference. Sometimes they just don’t know where to direct that support — or they haven’t had the opportunity to do so in a tangible way. 💫Today, you do. Our team is honored to be part of the Stanford Day of Giving, which opens TODAY — Wednesday, May 13 at 5 AM Pacific Time — and there is a MATCH at stake. Your support will directly help advance life-saving, life-changing work focused on making access to care and clinical outcomes for non-communicable diseases more equitable across Africa, with a special focus on Kenya. This work is deeply personal, deeply human, and deeply necessary. From hypertension to diabetes to cancer and chronic lung disease, non-communicable diseases are rising rapidly across the continent — yet access to timely diagnosis, treatment, emergency care, and long-term support remains profoundly unequal. Our lab is working to change that through research, advocacy, systems strengthening, and partnerships grounded in equity and local leadership. Learn more about our work here: https://lnkd.in/g5XnJrsu If you’d like to support us during Stanford Day of Giving: ➡️ Go to the following website: https://lnkd.in/d9S36rp6 ➡️ Click the “Give Now!” button at the top of the page ➡️ Select Stanford Medicine from the Category dropdown menu ➡️ Click the plus button next to Other Stanford Medicine Designation to add the fund to your cart ➡️ Adjust the gift amount as desired ➡️ Click Continue ➡️ Under Additional Details, enter: “Department of Emergency Medicine - Dr. Christine Ngaruiya lab fund” Every GIFT matters. Every SHARE matters. Every PERSON who joins this effort helps move us closer to a world where someone lives does not determine whether they survive, thrive, and have access to the care they deserve. Thank you for believing in this work — and for standing with us in community! CC: Sean Maher , Jessica Rayo , Dr. Loice Wanjiru Cushny-Kaigwa #globalhealth #NCDs #globalhealth #healthequity #equity #noncommunicabledisease #cancer #heartdisease #stroke #tobaccocessation #lunghealth #climatechange Stanford University ...more ...more

We built a system that lets multiple people construct a city using only their brain signals! In just 48 hours Siddharth Manne , Emiliano Cuevas , and I built Inception - a multi-brain collaborative city generator - at the Global Neurohack Hackathon hosted at the frontiertower bringing teams around the world from Oxford University, UC Berkeley, Rice, Imperial, and more. No keyboards. No mice. No talking. Just brains. Multiple people wear OpenBCI EEG headsets simultaneously. Their combined neural signals detect emotional state in real time and that collective emotion continuously shapes the atmosphere, color, and feel of the world being built. We use neural symbiosis where not just one brain commands a machine, but multiple minds fuse together. Your brain sets the mood. Your eyes place the objects. Your voice summons the architecture. You speak a scene out loud, Black Forest Labs generates an image, that image is animated into a video, and Meta's TRIBE v2 - trained on 500+ hours of fMRI scans from 700+ people - predicts the exact neural activation pattern for what you're perceiving and decodes what gets built next. Through ElevenLabs, the city finds its voice, narrating the world as it dreams itself into existence. The bigger picture: everyone is stuck navigating 2D menus to express 3D ideas. We built a system where you don't describe what you want to build — you feel it, look at it, and speak it into existence. When design tools finally speak the language of human thought rather than forcing human thought to speak the language of design tools, the barriers between imagination and creation dissolve. That's the world we're building toward. Huge thanks to the organizers and shoutout to some awesome people we met during the hackathon: Matthew MacDougall , Luke Gordon , Morgan Hough, and more. Check it out here: https://lnkd.in/gFQjtuNK ...more

Most diabetes patients must carefully monitor their blood sugar levels and inject insulin multiple times per day. As a possible alternative to those injections, MIT researchers are developing an implantable device that contains insulin-producing cells. This device, the researchers hope, could offer a way to achieve long-term control of type 1 diabetes. https://lnkd.in/em4qvQ67 ...more ...more

For the conversation, we’re bringing together leaders across AI, VC, tech, policy, and the creative economy, including a fireside chat with Emmanuel Lubanzadio, Africa Lead at OpenAI. Highlights include: Panels across the creative sector, policy, and tech startups A fireside chat with Emmanuel Lubanzadio, Africa Lead at OpenAI A post-event networking mixer bringing together GSB students and alums 🎟 There’s also a raffle for attendees to join Emmanuel for a private dinner after the event. Open to the public. Tickets close Feb 20. ...more

Excited to share that a project I worked on in high school was just published in Nature! I worked with Prof. Howard Chang, Prof. Siddhartha Jaiswal, and Dr. Julia Belk at Stanford’s School of Medicine to research how mitochondrial DNA mutations can be used to trace macrophage lineage across tissues. It was amazing to see how this project expanded after I moved on to college, eventually spanning multiple labs and contributors. When I was a lot younger, being part of a Nature paper seemed like the coolest thing a scientist could do; like something I’d daydream about while I sat for hours at a flow cytometer. This is an absolutely surreal feeling. I’m extremely grateful to my mentor, Julia Belk , for guiding me through this journey and teaching me what it takes to get research through to publication. https://lnkd.in/gzU6D_Wh

What an incredible journey! ​After three unforgettable years at École Polytechnique , I am beyond thrilled to share that I have officially graduated with a 𝗕.𝗦𝗰 𝗱𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗷𝗼𝗿 𝗶𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗵𝘆𝘀𝗶𝗰𝘀! ​These past few years gave me so much more than a diploma. They completely transformed how I tackle complex problems, blending rigorous mathematical reasoning with physical intuition and a truly multidisciplinary mindset. ​A massive highlight of this adventure? Spending a semester abroad at KAIST in South Korea. Adapting, thriving, and immersing myself in a brand-new environment pushed me to grow in ways I never imagined—both personally and intellectually. ​I’m also immensely proud of my Bachelor’s thesis on Exotic 2D Sn Lattices on Ag(111), conducted at the Institut des nanosciences de Paris ( CNRS – Sorbonne Université ). Contributing to cutting-edge quantum surface science was a fascinating experience, and I am deeply grateful to my supervisor Romain Bernard, and to Geoffroy Prévot , for their incredible mentorship and generosity. I can’t wait to see our team's research published soon! ​And the adventure doesn't stop here... ​I am excited to announce that I am heading to Yale University to pursue my 𝗠𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝗣𝗵𝘆𝘀𝗶𝗰𝘀! I can’t wait to learn from world-class researchers and dive into Yale’s vibrant ecosystem—especially at the Yale Quantum Institute , where fundamental science discoveries meets innovative real-world impact. ​Thrilled to start this next chapter! Here's to new challenges, new collaborations, and New Haven! 😉 #Graduation #ÉcolePolytechnique #Yale #AppliedPhysics #Physics #Math #Mathematics #Quantum #Research
